clue.text: Knowledge sphere to take to higher academic level?

definitions.meaning: a field or area of learning, a subject someone is expert in

definitions.text: to take to higher academic level?
definitions.meaning: read as three little words: to 'do' a master's degree 'in' a subject is to pursue it to postgraduate level

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the answer as DO MA IN, as in 'to do an MA in history', and the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere of knowledge is a field of study, and studying for a master's degree in that field takes it further academically.

clue.text: Race in the Americas in field, wearing socks

indicators.note: the field is dressed in the socks, so it sits inside them

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them, so 'socks' can mean chins, as in hits on the chin
lea is an old poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A footballer in South America plays on the pitch in socks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Socks' looks like clothing for the field to wear, but it is the verb meaning punches; 'wearing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Chile, a South American nation, are a people of the Americas.

clue.text: Plant spies outside game

indicators.note: the spies stand around the game, enclosing it

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies
a lark is a bit of fun or a game

explanation.surface: Agents lurk around a sports field watching a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkia is a genus of flowering annuals from western North America.

clue.text: Sport where there's no time for messing

indicators.note: no time means the word for messing loses its T

parts.note: tangling hair or string is messing it up

explanation.surface: A pastime in which nobody has a moment to waste fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing' gives TANGLING, and 'no time' removes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line is a popular sport and pastime.

clue.text: Different books, now abridged

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the word for now loses its last letter

parts.note: here, as in 'here and now', can mean at present

explanation.surface: A new edition of some books has now been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' cuts HERE to HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means not the same, distinct or alternative.

clue.text: A place like Cheltenham in the fifties: old woman's resort

indicators.note: the A and the spa go inside the pair of fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties make LL
Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, England, is a famous spa town
ma's is mother's, one's 'old woman' being slang for one's mother

explanation.surface: A nostalgic memory of a genteel English spa town in the 1950s and an elderly lady's holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English spa town in Gloucestershire; 'in' puts the A and spa between the two Roman fifties, and the old woman follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas, on Gran Canaria in the Canary Islands, is a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: How airlock affected one hooked to post?

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how an airlock affected a person stuck on a mail stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' rearranges HOW AIRLOCK; 'post' means a job, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted to their job, unable to stop toiling, is hooked on their position.

clue.text: Champ, furthermore, not heard by many?

indicators.note: the question mark and 'many' admit that only those who drop the R say it this way, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: nor means 'and not', furthermore plus a negative

explanation.surface: A boxing champion, the speaker adds, goes unheard by most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' is a verb meaning chew noisily, not a champion. 'Heard by many' signals the sound-alike: NOR said by speakers who drop the R matches the answer, whose G is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or chew vigorously, as a horse does its bit.

clue.text: Scandinavian staff a local shows round

indicators.note: round means the run of letters is turned to read backwards
the clue words show the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A local person shows off his walking stick to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' points to letters found in STAFF A LOCAL; 'round' turns FALO back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Olaf is a common Norwegian and Danish man's name, borne by several kings of Norway.

clue.text: Large grant aid's transformed major battle scene

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the letters of aid's are used with the apostrophe dropped, giving the S

explanation.surface: A big grant of foreign aid has changed a war-torn place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges L, GRANT and AIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet city was the site of a decisive and bloody battle of the Second World War in 1942-43.

clue.text: Don cape when meeting a dance star of the East End

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
a ball is a formal dance
a hero is a star; a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, saying 'ero

explanation.surface: Put on a cloak to meet a dancer who is a local celebrity in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the verb put on but is the Spanish title. Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their H's, so a HERO becomes 'ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gentleman is styled Don, and a caballero is a Spanish gentleman or knight.

clue.text: Bone that is broken in accident, initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A bone that gets broken in an accident at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: A little old book one's into about the facts of life

indicators.note: into puts the numeral within the other letters
about means the run of pieces before it is turned around

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
I is the Roman numeral one; 'one's into' says it is placed inside

explanation.surface: A small antique volume explains the birds and the bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns A TAD O B round to BODATA, and 'into' puts I inside it after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Biographical details, a person's life history in summary, are literally the facts of a life.

clue.text: Girl's posh, clad in fancy clothes

definitions.note: girl's here is short for girl is

indicators.note: used as a verb, clothes means wraps around, so the rearranged letters surround the posh letter
fancy means elaborate or imagined, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A girl is smart, wearing elaborate garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' is a verb, not the noun it seems: the anagram of CLAD IN (signalled by 'fancy') clothes U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucinda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Suffers with kidney, to be brief

parts.note: to take something, such as an insult, is to suffer or endure it
kidney means sort or type, as does ilk: 'of that kidney'

explanation.surface: A patient endures trouble with a kidney, to put it shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be brief' looks like 'in short', but a brief is a barrister; in Britain a barrister who becomes a King's or Queen's Counsel is said to take silk, from the silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a senior barrister, a leading counsel, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Sources of wood and metal from the sea

parts.note: the ash tree is one source of timber
ore is rock from which metal is extracted, sharing 'sources of'

explanation.surface: Where timber and iron come from, delivered by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sources of' serves both: ash is a source of wood, ore a source of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming onto land out of the water, as a sailor or washed-up item does.

clue.text: Cook that's making TV show

parts.note: to cook the books is to doctor them, falsify them
who, as a relative pronoun, can stand for that

explanation.surface: A chef who stars in a television cookery programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef, but it means falsify, as in cooking the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC science fiction series is a television programme.

clue.text: County hospital after food

indicators.note: after means the hospital letter comes behind the food

parts.note: meat is food, as in 'meat and drink'
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A local hospital serves a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meath is a county in the Republic of Ireland, north-west of Dublin.

clue.text: Person drawing, perhaps, on crew for Crimean battle

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the crew word is placed below, after

parts.note: an inker is one who inks drawings, such as comic art, so a person drawing, perhaps
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: An artist joins a ship's company to record a war in the Crimea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman, in the Crimea, was the site of an 1854 battle in the Crimean War.

clue.text: Dire warning from teacher to revolve around drink

indicators.note: the teacher and revolving words go around the drink

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
to roll is to turn over and over, to revolve
swill can mean drink greedily, or drink as a noun

explanation.surface: A headmaster threatens a pupil who staggers around after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' makes the teacher and the revolving word wrap the drink, one on each side; 'to revolve' is a verb phrase, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom threatening that people will be punished or sacked, from executions by beheading.

clue.text: Hold-up of entry — something you'll not get today?

parts.note: a log is a record, made of entries; an entry in it is logged
from Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass: 'jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam today'

explanation.surface: A diary entry notes a delay, a treat you will not receive today.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen in Through the Looking-Glass offers 'jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam today'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockage, as of timber in a river or traffic on a road, causes a delay or obstruction.

clue.text: Turkey portion, once yours truly's home, when men need to eat

indicators.note: the soldiers and when word must eat, so they surround the speaker's phrase

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers, hence men
yours truly is the speaker, so 'yours truly's' means I am
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Turkey's history, once the speaker's home, when soldiers had to be fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' is the country, not a bird; 'once' marks the name as historical. 'Need to eat' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient name for Anatolia, the western peninsula that forms most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: Sounds relieved, maybe, with volume coming through speakers?

indicators.note: what comes through speakers is spoken aloud, so the word is the sound of the volume word

parts.note: volume can mean size, the space something takes up

explanation.surface: A loud noise comes over the hi-fi, expressing relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speakers' looks like hi-fi loudspeakers, but it means people speaking: SIZE said aloud matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out audibly from relief, a long deep exhalation, is one way to show it.

clue.text: What we'd often like to be that, mostly, only a few'll become

definitions.text: What we'd often like to be

indicators.note: become means turn into something else, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word that, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the letters of few'll are used without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something most of us wish we were, that only a handful will ever be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' shortens THAT to THA, and 'become' rearranges THA with ONLY A FEW'LL. The phrase means an unseen observer of private events.
explanation.definitionFit: Many people wish they could secretly observe things unnoticed, like an insect perched on a partition.

clue.text: Barrier out of line stopping back door moving

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the line letter goes inside
moving means the letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A barricade cut off from the rest, blocking the rear entrance from opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the doorway words to ROADBOCK, and 'stopping' plugs the line letter into it; 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A police barricade across a road, or any obstruction to progress, is a barrier.

clue.text: Something worn on one's head or on one's toes?

definitions.meaning: a wide-brimmed soft felt hat of the 19th century bore this name

explanation.definitionFit: A low-crowned broad-brimmed felt hat bore the name, and the phrase also means fully alert.

clue.text: Takes chances boxing heavyweight after upsetting gags!

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the gambling word holds the heavyweight

parts.note: to dice, as in 'dice with death', is to take risks

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means turning the word upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A gambler boxes a heavyweight after jokes go down badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gags' are not jokes but British press censorship orders. 'After upsetting' turns the heavyweight to NOT, and 'boxing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: British government notices asking editors not to publish items on national security act as restraints on the press.

clue.text: Invariably as well to be brief describing fashion

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line around, so the shortened word encloses the fashion word
to be brief means shortened, so the word for as well loses its last letter

parts.note: also means as well, too
a way is a manner or fashion of doing something

explanation.surface: Being concise always works well when talking about style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be brief' cuts the last letter, leaving ALS, and 'describing' (drawing a line round) signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean on every occasion, without exception.

clue.text: At the outset, control a program that uses Internet Explorer

indicators.note: at the outset means the opening letter of control is taken

parts.note: a bot is a software robot that runs automated tasks over the web

explanation.surface: A computer program that controls a web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Internet Explorer' looks like the web browser, but the explorer stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was a Venetian navigator who reached North America in 1497 for England.

clue.text: Instrument provided by girl replacing daughter in orchestra

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the place of the daughter letter

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is supplied by a young woman standing in for a daughter in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument with a round drum-like body.
